To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
synthetic tethered ligand (STL) agonists are highly potent and specific activators of the G protein‐coupled receptor protease‐activated receptors 2 (PAR2).
the synthetic lipid‐tethered ligands (SLT‐LIGRL) represent the most potent PAR2 agonists reported to date, with EC50 values as high as 200‐fold lower than that reported for the untethered ligand.
the tethered ligands developed in our research represent a new class of potent and specific PAR2 agonists that have potential for the treatment of pain and inflammation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of highly potent PAR2 agonists.
the design, synthesis and biological evaluation of novel PAR2‐targeted therapeutics.
the development of a novel class of highly potent and selective PAR2 agonists that may have therapeutic value in the treatment of pain, inflammatory disorders and other diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the authors have successfully demonstrated that tethered ligands are an effective means of enhancing the affinity of PAR2 ligands, and that this approach can be applied to other G protein-coupled receptors.
the synthetic lipid tethering approach is a powerful method to improve ligand potency at protease activated receptors (PARs), and potentially across G protein coupled receptors (GPCRs).
we have successfully demonstrated that the STL approach can be used for improving ligand potency at a GPCR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new strategy to improve ligand potency at G‐protein coupled receptors.
we have developed a new approach for improving potency at protease‐activated receptors (PARs) and across GPCRS.
we have developed the first highly potent synthetic agonists of PAR2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synthetic tethering of a PAR2 agonist to a lipid dramatically improves potency and efficacy in vivo.
lipidation of PAR2 agonists significantly improves potency and selectivity in vitro and in vivo.
the lipidation strategy can significantly increase the potency of PAR2 agonists, which may be useful in developing therapeutics to target PAR2.
